cohort: The study included 100 pregnant patients with high-risk conditions such as PIH, diabetes, IUGR, or diminished fetal movements, and a gestational age between 33 and 42 weeks, excluding normal pregnancies, multifetal pregnancies, or those with congenital fetal anomalies.
finding: Abnormal admission cardiotocography (CTG) results were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of caesarean section, lower birth weight (less than 2.5 kg), and lower 1-minute APGAR scores (7 or less), suggesting its utility as a reliable fetal monitoring screening technique.
mod_finding: Abnormal admission CTG results were significantly associated with a higher likelihood of caesarean section delivery (92.59% of abnormal CTG group had CS, compared to 42.47% of normal CTG group having spontaneous delivery).
birth_weight: Analysis included categories less than 2.5 kg and over 2.5 kg.
